blockNote: Per-scene hub thinker (Bank 00, 49035-49577, about 545 bytes), spawned in about 60 scene_thinkers lists, usually as the last slot. It has two jobs: it loads the player's sprite palette for the current form once at spawn, and it runs the shared 'talk to the thing in front of you' interaction every frame. It is not an ambient effect, and the trigger is the interact bit of joypadCurrent, not a direction press as the old header said.
=== PALETTE (spawn only) ===

SwitchCase on characterForm ($0AD4: 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow; no range check, so the table's fourth entry is never reached) runs PaletteStart / PaletteStep on bundle #0B (Will), #0C (Freedan) or #23 (Shadow). All three write colours $81-$8F, which is OBJ palette 0 colours 1-15, the player's sprite palette. #0B and #0C are a single static strip; #23 is an animated set of strips (wait 2 each). PaletteStep plays the whole bundle before the script continues. The palette is chosen once when the thinker spawns, so a form change in the middle of a scene is not re-applied until the next scene setup.
=== FILTER WORD ===

thinker-def <#00, #08> gives animScratch2 = $0800 (bit 11 set: also run in the Light runners). GlobalAmbientInteractEntry clears bit 11 in the thinker's own animScratch2, so from then on the dispatcher runs only in RunThinkers_General (the main loop) and is skipped by the lighter frame routines (dialogue, render, music upload): no new talk starts while a dialogue frame loop is running. The old comment called bit 11 an 'interaction ready flag'.
=== TALK INTERACTION (every frame) ===

1. PHD / TCD set D = 0 and joypadCurrent bit $8000 is tested: the interact bit. In the vanilla layout it is the B button (remapB); in this build transforms.json rewrites the system_init defaults to remapA = $8080 and remapB = $4008, so the A button feeds it (together with the attack bit $0080). The notes in this file name the logical bit, not a button. Not pressed: return.
2. GetPlayerFacingDirection: carry SET = no valid facing, return; carry CLEAR = valid, so the label GlobalAmbientFacingInvalid is the VALID path. A = 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right, saved in $09EE.

3. A probe point one pixel in front of the player ($18 / $1C = player X / Y plus (0,+1), (0,-1), (-1,0) or (+1,0)) is built. The four scan labels are rotated against their names: GlobalAmbientScanEast handles facing 0 (down), ScanWest facing 1 (up), ScanNorth facing 2 (left), ScanSouth facing 3 (right).

4. GlobalAmbientFindActorInFront walks the actor list from actorListFirst and keeps the actor with the smallest |dx| + |dy| to the probe point whose |dx| and |dy| are both below $10 and whose sum is below $20. Only actors with Flags10 bit $1000 count (the third actor-def header byte of NPCs and objects carries it; the player has it clear and is skipped). X = 0 when none is found.

5. The target is 'in front' when its coordinate along the facing axis is beyond the probe (GlobalAmbientTargetInRange), otherwise it is at or behind the player (GlobalAmbientTargetBehindPlayer). Both need a non-zero chatPtr ($7F000A, set by SetInteractHandler). A target at or behind the player runs its chat routine directly; a target in front first sets the interact bit in joypadHeld.

6. In front and Flags12 ($12) bit $0200 clear: the turn-and-talk path (GlobalAmbientPlayTalkSound, which plays no sound despite the name). The target's actor slot ($30 bytes, bank 0) and its extended $7F page ($30 bytes) are copied to $7E:3410-$346F through the RAM MVN stub at $0402 ($0404 = destination bank, $0405 = source bank, A = $2F is the byte count minus one, not a sound number; the old comments called it SFX $2F). The target is then turned to face the player (GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame), its animation is updated at once, its chat routine runs as a subroutine and, when it returns, both copies are written back (GlobalAmbientTalkSoundResume). WRAM flags, dialogue and inventory changes made by the chat routine persist, but the NPC's own actor fields (position, animation, entry pointer, flags) are put back as they were; the next-link $06 is kept as it is now when the saved copy had none (it was the list tail).
7. Flags12 bit $0200 set (over 150 NPC, sign, book and door actor scripts set it) skips the snapshot, the turn and the animation: the chat routine runs directly (GlobalAmbientDeferToScript).
8. GlobalAmbientClearTalkInput then clears the interact bit in joypadCurrent and sets it in joypadHeld so the same press cannot trigger again.

GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame turns the target to face the player: it picks offset 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right of the target's 8-frame animation group, the OPPOSITE of the player's facing, and adds it to the group base ((index - 2) AND $FFF8) + 2. It overwrites $09EE with that offset; the label GlobalAmbientAnimFacingVertical is the left / right branch.
The interaction code uses the global direct page scratch $00-$04, $18 and $1C (D = 0); none of those is part of the persistent engine state.

partNotes.GlobalAmbientDispatchEntry: Spawn entry: pick the player's sprite palette bundle by characterForm ($0AD4). Runs once per scene setup.
partNotes.code_list_00BF91: SwitchCase table by characterForm: 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow; entry 3 is never reached (the form is 0-2).
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPaletteWill: Will: bundle #0B, OBJ palette 0 colours $81-$8F (static), then the interaction loop.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPaletteFreedan: Freedan: bundle #0C, OBJ palette 0 colours $81-$8F (static), then the interaction loop.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPaletteShadow: Shadow: bundle #23, an animated strip set on the same colours, then the interaction loop.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPaletteDefault: Index 3, never reached (characterForm is 0-2): the same bundle as Freedan.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientInteractEntry: Per-frame loop head. Clears bit 11 of animScratch2 so the thinker leaves the Light runners (no talk starts during dialogue / render / music-upload frames), yields, and tests the interact bit with D = 0.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientOnDirectionPress: Interact bit pressed (the old name says direction press). Read the player's facing, build the probe point in front of the player and find the interactable actor there.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientFacingInvalid: VALID-facing path despite the name (BCC after GetPlayerFacingDirection: carry clear = valid). Saves the facing in $09EE and splits into the four probe builders.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientScanEast: Facing 0 = DOWN (not east): probe point = player X, player Y + 1.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientScanWest: Facing 1 = UP (not west): probe point = player X, player Y - 1.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientScanNorth: Facing 2 = LEFT (not north): probe point = player X - 1, player Y.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientScanSouth: Facing 3 = RIGHT (not south): probe point = player X + 1, player Y.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientNoTargetFound: No actor near the probe point: restore P and D and return; the press is left in joypadCurrent.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientTargetBehindPlayer: Target at or behind the player along the facing axis (the signed difference to the probe went negative): needs a chatPtr, then runs it directly.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientInvokeLinkedScript: Make the target the current direct page (TXA / TCD) and run its chat routine through GlobalAmbientDeferToScript.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientTargetInRange: Target beyond the probe (in front of the player): mark the interact bit as held, require a chatPtr, then either the direct call (Flags12 $0200 set) or the turn-and-talk snapshot path.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientDeferToScript: Direct call of the target's chat routine: push the return address (GlobalAmbientClearTalkInput), the actor's bank ($02) and chatPtr - 1, set the interact bit in joypadHeld and RTL into it.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPlayTalkSound: Turn-and-talk path (no sound is played): snapshot the target's actor slot and $7F page to $7E:3410-$346F with the RAM MVN stub $0402, turn the target to face the player, then call its chat routine with GlobalAmbientTalkSoundResume as the return address.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientClearTalkInput: Consume the press: clear the interact bit in joypadCurrent, set it in joypadHeld, restore P and D and return.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientTalkSoundResume: Return point of the turn-and-talk path: write the snapshot back to the target's actor slot and $7F page (keeping the live next-link $06 when the saved one was 0), then consume the press.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientFindActorInFront: Actor scan around the probe point ($18 / $1C): Flags10 bit $1000 required, |dx| and |dy| below $10, sum below $20; returns the nearest in X (0 = none) with Z set accordingly. Scratch: $00 = |dx|, $02 = best distance (starts at $20), $04 = best actor.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientPickTalkAnimFrame: Return in A the animation index that turns the target to face the player: the group base ((index - 2) AND $FFF8) + 2 plus the opposite-of-the-player's-facing offset (down 0, up 1, left 2, right 3). Overwrites $09EE with the offset.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientAnimFacingVertical: Despite the name this is the LEFT / RIGHT branch (facing 2 or 3): 2 -> offset 3, 3 -> offset 2.
partNotes.GlobalAmbientAnimFacingApply: Store the offset in $09EE and add it to the group base of the target's current animation index.

blockNote: Elliptical orbit offset (Bank 00, 62514-62606). It ADDS an offset to the actor's own position ($14 / $16), computed from two independent angle / diameter pairs in the actor's extended WRAM page, so the caller must first write the orbit centre into $14 / $16 before every call (otherwise the offset accumulates). gw8A_sand_fanger reloads the centre from moveXAlt / moveYAlt, awB1_goldcap from its own WRAM fields.

Fields, one byte each, indexed by X = actor slot ($7F0010 + X ...): +0 X angle, +1 Y angle, +2 X diameter, +3 Y diameter. orbitAngle and orbitDiameter are the word views of the two pairs (low byte = X, high byte = Y). One angle step is 1.40625 degrees (256 per turn).

X offset = (|sine_table_8bit[angleX]| x diameterX) >> 8 with the sign of the table value; Y offset = the same with signed_cosine_table_8bit[angleY] and diameterY. The table peak is $7F, so each offset is about +/- diameter / 2 and the diameter is the full width of the ellipse. With equal angles the point starts below the centre (sine 0, cosine at its peak, Y grows downward) and moves right, then up, then left: counter-clockwise on screen. Different angle rates give Lissajous paths.

The sign travels in the carry flag from the table lookup through Multiply8x8Unsigned, which preserves carry. The routine clobbers A, Y and the flags; X (the actor slot) and D are preserved. It ends with A and the index registers 16-bit.

Callers (3 sites): gw8A_sand_fanger (2) and awB1_goldcap (1, where the X diameter grows by 3 and the Y diameter by 2 per step so the path spirals outward). The old header also listed statue_inventory_reward, which uses ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef instead.

62514.text: X angle (low byte of orbitAngle); the high byte is the Y angle, read below via $7F0011

62525.text: sine_table_8bit[angleX]: the magnitude is multiplied by the diameter, the sign is kept in carry

62530.text: Negative table value: take the magnitude (EOR #$FF, INC) and remember the sign in carry (SEC)

62535.text: X diameter (low byte of orbitDiameter): A = diameter, B = |sine|

62539.text: Unsigned A x B; carry (the sign) is preserved

62545.text: High byte of the product = |sine| x diameter / 256

62549.text: Carry set (negative sine): negate the offset

62556.text: X position += offset (the caller put the orbit centre in $14)

62571.text: signed_cosine_table_8bit[angleY]: the Y axis uses the cosine table

62602.text: Y position += offset: the actor ends at centre + (dx, dy)

blockNote: Palette-phase thinker of the Gold Ship wreck scenes (Bank 00, 46705-46802). The old name and notes say 'Incan Ruins', but the three scene_thinkers lists that spawn it are $2B (ship wreck), $2D (ship wreck interior) and $2F (adrift), all Gold Ship scenes, and the flags it reads, $4D and $52, are set and cleared by dc2F_adrift (also gs2E_sleep and gs2B_erik). The old doc claims about Larai Cliff / Angkor and scene indexes 34-36 are wrong.
=== PHASE PICK (spawn only) ===

The two flag tests run once when the thinker spawns; the loops after them never return to the tests, so the phase is fixed for the scene visit (scene $2F reloads for each adrift 'day', which re-spawns the thinker with the then-current flags). Flag $52 set: final phase. Else flag $4D set: warm phase. Neither: default.
=== DEFAULT: bundle #1A forever ===

A 12-strip palette cycle on colours $21-$2C (palette 2, colours 1-12): each strip is a 24-byte window that slides one colour at a time (wait 2-5), the peak colour $4164 a bright blue, so a highlight travels through the 12 colours. PaletteStart + PaletteStep play all strips and BRA repeats. It reads as a water glint cycle (an inference from the colours).
=== FLAG $4D: IncanRuinsTransformPaletteWarmup ===

Bundle #34 once (a one-shot: 16 colours at $70, palette 7, and one colour at $59), then the scene-setup latch $FF is set and bundle #33 (the same 12-strip cycle as #1A with other colour values) loops while $FF stays set. When the latch is cleared (next scene setup or inventory open) the thinker restarts with #34. The old note 'alternate between #34 and #33' is wrong: #34 plays once per latch cycle.
=== FLAG $52: IncanRuinsTransformPaletteFinal ===

Kills the thinker at the list head ($5A) and the one in the next pool slot (+$10): the first two thinkers spawned, which are scanline_band_hdma_thinker records 0 and 1 in all three lists (pool slots are handed out in ascending order from $0F00). KillThinker works on the slot in X and uses D only for its operand pointer, so D can stay on this thinker. Then it fills palette-buffer bytes $7F0A40-$7F0A5F, colours $20-$2F (palette 2), with $1421 (very dark blue, R1 G1 B5) so the colours the cycle used stay flat, sets colour 0 ($7F0A00) to $1442, applies bundle #36 (17 colours at $50, 16 at $70), sets $FF and waits for the latch to clear before repeating the fill and #36 (the kills are not repeated). The old 'CGRAM entries $40-$5F' are buffer byte offsets.
What $4D and $52 mean in story terms (adrift day / night / starvation phase) and what the colours depict is not decoded (OQ-I044-1).
